preamble: Shift of the labiodental fricative [f] to the bilabial fricative [ɸ]. In Māori, Proto-Polynesian *f became the sound written wh, traditionally bilabial [ɸ] (*fale 'house' > whare), although many modern speakers use [f].

examples.note: Māori wh, from *f, is traditionally bilabial [ɸ]; many speakers now use [f]

sources: Ladefoged, P., & Maddieson, I. (1996). The Sounds of the World's Languages. Blackwell. https://www.wiley.com/en-us/The+Sounds+of+the+World%27s+Languages-p-9780631198154
Campbell, L. (2013). Historical Linguistics: An Introduction (3rd ed.). Edinburgh University Press; MIT Press. https://lccn.loc.gov/2012038044
Harlow, R. (2007). Māori: A Linguistic Introduction. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511618697
